column2: Which figure diagrams for my family (ranking, streams, histogram, box, dumbbells, figure cards…)?
column3: In “＋ New diagram”, “Figures” group: 🏁 the changing ranking (the most given first names, decade by decade: the app calculates the ranks from the numbers); 🌊 stacked streams (the family’s occupations over 200 years); 📶 the histogram (type or paste raw values, for example ages at death: the app sorts them into bins whose width you choose); 📦 the box plot (median, quartiles and outliers calculated for each group, for example age at marriage by century); 🏋️ dumbbells (two values per row: the husband’s and the wife’s age); ↗️ the before / after slope; 🪜 the waterfall (a total that goes up and down, with subtotals); 🍭 🍡 horizontal or vertical lollipops; 🐝 the beeswarm (one person = one point, their name on hover); 🔲 small line charts in a grid (same scale or not). “Key figures” group: 🔢 figure cards (a big number, the arrow and the change from the previous value, a mini line, a colour according to your thresholds) and 🎯 the target bar (value, target and zones, for example “64% of ancestors found in the 8th generation”). The “From the app” tab → “🌳 Data from my tree” fills them with your database: ages at death and at marriage, first names, occupations, births by name or by commune, database counters, ancestors found per generation.

column2: How do I see my DNA as a diagram (painted chromosomes, cM ruler)?
column3: In “＋ New diagram”, “DNA” group: 🧬 chromosome painting (the 22 pairs and the X, one bar for the copy received from the father and one for the mother’s; each segment shared with a cousin is painted, coloured by branch, by cousin or by side; at the top, the share of the genome already painted) and 📏 the cM ruler (each match is a point on a cM scale, under which the ranges of relationships from the Shared cM Project are lined up; write a name in “Show the possible relationships of…” to see the most likely ones in %). “From the app” tab: choose the tested person then their test, the app takes the segments or matches from the DNA tab. A click on a segment or a point opens the cousin’s record if they are in your tree. Without a test in the app, fill in or paste the table (chromosome, start, end, cM, cousin, side, branch).

column2: What other figure diagrams are there (ridgelines, mosaic, dot plot, Nightingale rose, occupational mobility)?
column3: In “＋ New diagram”: 🏔️ ridgelines (Figures group: one curve per century or per sex, overlapping like mountains, for example age at death; click on a ridge: the list of people); ⚫ the dot plot (one point per series on the same line, for example the average age at death of women and men by commune); 🔁 the mobility table (the father’s occupation in rows, the son’s or daughter’s in columns, each cell darker when it is frequent, framed when it is the same occupation; occupations can be grouped into families; click on a cell: the people); Slices group: 🧱 the variable-width mosaic (each column is wider the bigger its total, for example occupations century by century) and 🌹 the Nightingale rose (one slice per month, its area follows the figure, series stacked or overlaid: births, marriages, deaths or conceptions). “From the app” → “🌳 Data from my tree” fills them with your database.

column2: Diagrams: what do the options in “From the app → Chart” mean?
column3: In a diagram’s editor, “From the app” tab: choose “🧮 Count in my database” in “Chart” (a ready-made starting point, or “Custom”), then set, always in the same order: what is counted (people, births, marriages, deaths, events, families, places, media; “each person only once” for events), the group of people (your whole database, your ancestors, your descendants, the paternal or maternal branch, a label, one of your lists, a search in the names or the people you choose), the period (from … to …, written as in a record), the grouping (surname, first name, sex, occupation, generation, commune, department, region, country, century, decade, year, month, age, number of children…), the series (by sex or by century, for stacked columns, the pyramid, the heat map), the sorting, the top N and “Others”, “Unknown” shown or hidden, the unit (number, %, average or median of age at death, age at marriage or number of children) and “🔄 Keep up to date” (the diagram is recalculated when your database changes). The sentence above the preview sums up the setting (“People born between 1800 and 1900, my ancestors, by department, top 10”). Each option has its “?” tooltip. The other types (maps, timelines, calendar, survival, occupations, marriages, tree figures…) keep their panel and gain the same group of people and the same period. An example, an app statistic or one of your charts can also be sorted, cut to the top N and switched to %. Your diagrams already made do not change.

column2: Which diagrams about life and death, couples, places and my research (child mortality, widowhood, signatures, proof…)?
column3: In “＋ New diagram”. “Life and death” group: 👶 Child mortality (by decade, the share of children who died before 1 year and before 5 years), 👨‍👩‍👧 Surviving siblings (for each couple: children born, reaching adulthood, dying young), 🗓 Seasons of births and deaths (month × period). “Couples and families” group: 💔 Widowhood and remarriage (the time before remarrying, men and women), ⏳ Length of marriages, 👴 Age of the parents at each birth (scatter plot), 🤰 Conceptions before marriage (first child born before the marriage or less than 8 months after), 💑 Age gap between spouses. “Places” group: 🧭 Far from the cradle (how far away the ancestors were born, generation by generation). “My research” group: ✍️ Able to sign, ✅ What you have proved (ancestors’ births, marriages and deaths with a source, without a source, not found), 📚 Registers consulted (the years seen and the gaps, according to the record index tracking and your sourced records). The “From the app” tab fills them with your database (without living people or confidential records), with the group of people and the period; a click on a bar or a point opens the list of people. The dark years, the incoming names, marriages between villages and the witnesses and godparents already existed: 📉 Births, deaths and crises, 🌳 Surname tree, 🎼 Chord diagram (marriages between villages) and 🕸️ Network of relationships (witnesses, godparents…).

column2: Which diagrams for a relationship, completeness, the ahnentafel, DNA (Leeds), the wheel of the year and two-axis figures?
column3: In “＋ New diagram”. “Genealogy” group: 🔗 the relationship path (choose two people: the shortest path step by step and the sentence “… is the second cousin of …”; in-laws and pedigree collapse are taken into account), 🧩 tree completeness (share of ancestors known in each generation, as bars or as a fan), 📜 the ancestry table (one row per Sosa number; “🖨 Print the table…” in “From the app”). “Maps” group: 🎯 the family’s centre of gravity (the average point of the places of birth of each generation and its path) and 🌈 the generations map. “DNA” group: 🧬 the Leeds matrix (your matches from 90 to 400 cM sorted by grandparent colour, from the DNA tab). “Timelines” group: 🎡 the wheel of the year (birthdays, marriages, deaths, name days). “Figures” group: 📊 bars + line (second axis on the right), ↔️ diverging bars, 🏔 stacked hills, 🧵 parallel coordinates, 📶 step line (how many in the family were alive, year by year). “🔒 For sharing” removes the names of living people; a confidential record is never named. A click on a box opens the record (or the list of people).

column2: How do I annotate a diagram (arrow, text, area, “WWI”)?
column3: In the diagram editor, “⚙️ Customise” tab → “✏️ Annotations”: ＋ Arrow, ＋ Text, ＋ Area, ＋ Vertical or horizontal band, ＋ Date marker (a date, or “from… to…” for a period). Drag them on the preview (and their small circles to enlarge them); double-click to change the text; Delete or × to remove them (“↶ Undo” right after). They are kept with the diagram, wherever it is placed, on export (PNG, SVG, PDF) and when printing.

column2: How do I give the same style to all my diagrams?
column3: “⚙️ Customise” tab → “🎨 Style”: a ready-made style (Plain, Archive, Bright colours, Printable black and white, Colour-blind) or your own (palette, font, background, line thickness, corners, text size, grid). “💾 My saved styles” keeps it under a name (and exports or imports it). “Apply to all diagrams” puts it on all of them (“↶ Undo” puts each one back as before); “⭐ Default style” gives it to new diagrams. “As before” removes the style.

column2: How do I compare side by side (small multiples), by sex, century, branch, place or generation?
column3: “⚙️ Customise” tab → “▦ Small multiples” → “Repeat the diagram by”: a small drawing per group, side by side, with the same scale. “The series in the table” works as soon as there are several columns of figures; for sex, century, branch, department, country or generation, first get your figures with “🧮 Count in my database” (“From the app” tab), ticking “Keep up to date”. For columns, bars, lines, areas, stacked and radar.

column2: How do I make a diagram scroll through time (▶ the years)?
column3: As soon as the data has dates (years as categories, timelines, members of a group, schedule…), a ▶ slider appears under the preview: play, speed (slow, normal, fast), loop, “⤢ All” to go back to the full drawing, and “🎬 Video” (WebM or MP4, depending on the browser). The scale does not move during playback. With “Reduce animations” (Settings → Accessibility), playback moves one step per second, without sliding. To show it also where the diagram is placed: “⚙️ Customise” → “▶ Playback over time”.

column2: How do I add an average, a median or a target to a chart?
column3: “⚙️ Customise” tab → “📏 Reference lines and axes” (columns, bars, stacked, lines, areas): ＋ Average, ＋ Median (calculated automatically, over all the series or just one), ＋ Target, ＋ Value. In the same place: “Logarithmic scale” for very large differences, and “Second axis (on the right)” to draw a series with its own scale.
